chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Why the all-night sessions with Farlow, Raney and Salvador were productive
summary: Playing among themselves allowed repeats and the exchange of ideas without audience pressure.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You mentioned very briefly the all night sessions you used to have in the New York with Tal Roney Farlow and Jimmy Rannie and Sal Salvador, talking and playing all night long. Did you find those kind of sessions just with eachother more stimulating and productive than had you been playing for audiences?

Oh, naturally, because we could do it over, you know. And we exchanged ideas, and it was just the-- you know, it wasn't a frantic thing where we just played. We played until we, you know, got tired and we'd stop, we'd talk, have coffee, or something, just play. It was just good fellowship, you know, and that was quite enjoyable. Yeah, I enjoyed it.
